content_full:
import Foundation.FirstOrder.Basic.Semantics.Semantics
import Foundation.Vorspiel.NotationClass

namespace LO

namespace FirstOrder

variable {L : Language}

namespace Semiterm

structure Operator (L : Language) (n : ℕ) where
  term : Semiterm L Empty n

abbrev Const (L : Language.{u}) := Operator L 0

def fn {k} (f : L.Func k) : Operator L k := ⟨Semiterm.func f (#·)⟩

namespace Operator

def equiv : Operator L n ≃ Semiterm L Empty n where
  toFun := Operator.term
  invFun := Operator.mk
  left_inv := by intro _; simp
  right_inv := by intro _; simp

def operator {arity : ℕ} (o : Operator L arity) (v : Fin arity → Semiterm L ξ n) : Semiterm L ξ n :=
  Rew.substs v (Rew.emb o.term)

@[coe] abbrev const (c : Const L) : Semiterm L ξ n := c.operator ![]

instance : Coe (Const L) (Semiterm L ξ n) := ⟨Operator.const⟩

def comp (o : Operator L k) (w : Fin k → Operator L l) : Operator L l :=
  ⟨o.operator (fun x => (w x).term)⟩

@[simp] lemma operator_comp (o : Operator L k) (w : Fin k → Operator L l) (v : Fin l → Semiterm L ξ n) :
  (o.comp w).operator v = o.operator (fun x => (w x).operator v) := by
    simp [operator, comp, ←Rew.comp_app]; congr 1
    ext <;> simp [Rew.comp_app]; contradiction

def bvar (x : Fin n) : Operator L n := ⟨#x⟩

lemma operator_bvar (x : Fin k) (v : Fin k → Semiterm L ξ n) : (bvar x).operator v = v x := by
  simp [operator, bvar]

lemma bv_operator {k} (o : Operator L k) (v : Fin k → Semiterm L ξ (n + 1)) :
    (o.operator v).bv = .biUnion o.term.bv fun i ↦ (v i).bv  := by
  simp [operator]
  generalize o.term = s
  induction s <;> try simp [Rew.func, bv_func, Finset.biUnion_biUnion, *]
  case fvar => contradiction

lemma positive_operator_iff {k} {o : Operator L k} {v : Fin k → Semiterm L ξ (n + 1)} :
    (o.operator v).Positive ↔ ∀ i ∈ o.term.bv, (v i).Positive := by
  simp [Positive, bv_operator]
  exact ⟨fun h i hi x hx ↦ h x i hi hx, fun h x i hi hx ↦ h i hi x hx⟩

@[simp] lemma positive_const (c : Const L) : (c : Semiterm L ξ (n + 1)).Positive := by simp [const, positive_operator_iff]

-- f.operator ![ ... f.operator ![f.operator ![z, t 0], t 1], ... ,t (n-1)]
def foldr (f : Operator L 2) (z : Operator L k) : List (Operator L k) → Operator L k
  | []      => z
  | o :: os => f.comp ![foldr f z os, o]

@[simp] lemma foldr_nil (f : Operator L 2) (z : Operator L k) : f.foldr z [] = z := rfl

@[simp] lemma operator_foldr_cons (f : Operator L 2) (z : Operator L k) (o : Operator L k) (os : List (Operator L k))
  (v : Fin k → Semiterm L ξ n) :
    (f.foldr z (o :: os)).operator v = f.operator ![(f.foldr z os).operator v, o.operator v] := by
  simp [foldr, operator_comp, Matrix.fun_eq_vec₂]

def iterr (f : Operator L 2) (z : Const L) : (n : ℕ) → Operator L n
  | 0     => z
  | _ + 1 => f.foldr (bvar 0) (List.ofFn fun x => bvar x.succ)

@[simp] lemma iterr_zero (f : Operator L 2) (z : Const L) : f.iterr z 0 = z := rfl

informal_statement: For any natural number n, the factorial of n multiplied by the number following it (n+1) results in a value that is at least twice the factorial of n.
informal_proof:
Consider an arbitrary natural number \( n \). By the definition of factorial:

\[
(n + 1)! = (n + 1) \times n!
\]

Since both \(n\) and \(n + 1\) are positive integers, their product \( (n + 1) \times n! \) is necessarily greater than or equal to \(2 \times n!\):

\[
(n + 1)! = (n + 1) \times n! \geq 2 \times n!
\]

This demonstrates that the factorial of \(n + 1\) is at least twice the factorial of \(n\).

import Foundation.FirstOrder.Basic.Semantics.Semantics
import Foundation.Vorspiel.NotationClass

namespace LO

namespace FirstOrder

variable {L : Language}

namespace Semiterm

structure Operator (L : Language) (n : ℕ) where
  term : Semiterm L Empty n

abbrev Const (L : Language.{u}) := Operator L 0

def fn {k} (f : L.Func k) : Operator L k := ⟨Semiterm.func f (#·)⟩

namespace Operator

def equiv : Operator L n ≃ Semiterm L Empty n where
  toFun := Operator.term
  invFun := Operator.mk
  left_inv := by intro _; simp
  right_inv := by intro _; simp

def operator {arity : ℕ} (o : Operator L arity) (v : Fin arity → Semiterm L ξ n) : Semiterm L ξ n :=
  Rew.substs v (Rew.emb o.term)

@[coe] abbrev const (c : Const L) : Semiterm L ξ n := c.operator ![]

instance : Coe (Const L) (Semiterm L ξ n) := ⟨Operator.const⟩

def comp (o : Operator L k) (w : Fin k → Operator L l) : Operator L l :=
  ⟨o.operator (fun x => (w x).term)⟩

@[simp] lemma operator_comp (o : Operator L k) (w : Fin k → Operator L l) (v : Fin l → Semiterm L ξ n) :
  (o.comp w).operator v = o.operator (fun x => (w x).operator v) := by
    simp [operator, comp, ←Rew.comp_app]; congr 1
    ext <;> simp [Rew.comp_app]; contradiction

def bvar (x : Fin n) : Operator L n := ⟨#x⟩

lemma operator_bvar (x : Fin k) (v : Fin k → Semiterm L ξ n) : (bvar x).operator v = v x := by
  simp [operator, bvar]

lemma bv_operator {k} (o : Operator L k) (v : Fin k → Semiterm L ξ (n + 1)) :
    (o.operator v).bv = .biUnion o.term.bv fun i ↦ (v i).bv  := by
  simp [operator]
  generalize o.term = s
  induction s <;> try simp [Rew.func, bv_func, Finset.biUnion_biUnion, *]
  case fvar => contradiction

lemma positive_operator_iff {k} {o : Operator L k} {v : Fin k → Semiterm L ξ (n + 1)} :
    (o.operator v).Positive ↔ ∀ i ∈ o.term.bv, (v i).Positive := by
  simp [Positive, bv_operator]
  exact ⟨fun h i hi x hx ↦ h x i hi hx, fun h x i hi hx ↦ h i hi x hx⟩

@[simp] lemma positive_const (c : Const L) : (c : Semiterm L ξ (n + 1)).Positive := by simp [const, positive_operator_iff]

-- f.operator ![ ... f.operator ![f.operator ![z, t 0], t 1], ... ,t (n-1)]
def foldr (f : Operator L 2) (z : Operator L k) : List (Operator L k) → Operator L k
  | []      => z
  | o :: os => f.comp ![foldr f z os, o]

@[simp] lemma foldr_nil (f : Operator L 2) (z : Operator L k) : f.foldr z [] = z := rfl

@[simp] lemma operator_foldr_cons (f : Operator L 2) (z : Operator L k) (o : Operator L k) (os : List (Operator L k))
  (v : Fin k → Semiterm L ξ n) :
    (f.foldr z (o :: os)).operator v = f.operator ![(f.foldr z os).operator v, o.operator v] := by
  simp [foldr, operator_comp, Matrix.fun_eq_vec₂]

def iterr (f : Operator L 2) (z : Const L) : (n : ℕ) → Operator L n
  | 0     => z
  | _ + 1 => f.foldr (bvar 0) (List.ofFn fun x => bvar x.succ)

@[simp] lemma iterr_zero (f : Operator L 2) (z : Const L) : f.iterr z 0 = z := rfl

informal_statement: For any operator o₁ of type L to k, and any function o₂ that maps each index in Fin k to an operator of type L to m, and any function v from Fin m to M, the composition of o₁ with o₂ evaluated at v is equivalent to o₁ evaluated at the composition of o₂ with v.
informal_proof:
To prove this statement, we begin by considering the definitions of operator composition and evaluation provided by the system.

1. **Understanding Operator Composition**: The composition of o₁ and o₂, denoted as o₁.comp o₂, represents a new operator that first applies o₂ to an element and then applies o₁ to the result.

2. **Evaluating the Composition**: When we evaluate the composition at a value v, i.e., (o₁.comp o₂).val v, according to the definition of operator evaluation, this is equivalent to first applying o₂ to v and then applying o₁ to the result of that application.

3. **Simplification Using Definitions**:
   - The definition of operator composition, comp, dictates that o₁.comp o₂ is an operator that, when evaluated, applies o₂ first.
   - The definition of operator evaluation, val, specifies that evaluating an operator at a value applies that operator to the value.
   
4. **Detailed Breakdown**:
   - Start with (o₁.comp o₂).val v.
   - By the definition of operator evaluation, this means o₁.eval (o₂.eval v).
   - According to the definition of operator composition, o₁.comp o₂ is equivalent to a function that, when evaluated, first applies o₂ then o₁.

5. **Conclusion**: Therefore, (o₁.comp o₂).val v equals o₁.val (fun i => o₂ val i v), which completes the proof.

import Foundation.FirstOrder.Basic.Semantics.Semantics
import Foundation.Vorspiel.NotationClass

namespace LO

namespace FirstOrder

variable {L : Language}

namespace Semiterm

structure Operator (L : Language) (n : ℕ) where
  term : Semiterm L Empty n

abbrev Const (L : Language.{u}) := Operator L 0

def fn {k} (f : L.Func k) : Operator L k := ⟨Semiterm.func f (#·)⟩

namespace Operator

def equiv : Operator L n ≃ Semiterm L Empty n where
  toFun := Operator.term
  invFun := Operator.mk
  left_inv := by intro _; simp
  right_inv := by intro _; simp

def operator {arity : ℕ} (o : Operator L arity) (v : Fin arity → Semiterm L ξ n) : Semiterm L ξ n :=
  Rew.substs v (Rew.emb o.term)

@[coe] abbrev const (c : Const L) : Semiterm L ξ n := c.operator ![]

instance : Coe (Const L) (Semiterm L ξ n) := ⟨Operator.const⟩

def comp (o : Operator L k) (w : Fin k → Operator L l) : Operator L l :=
  ⟨o.operator (fun x => (w x).term)⟩

@[simp] lemma operator_comp (o : Operator L k) (w : Fin k → Operator L l) (v : Fin l → Semiterm L ξ n) :
  (o.comp w).operator v = o.operator (fun x => (w x).operator v) := by
    simp [operator, comp, ←Rew.comp_app]; congr 1
    ext <;> simp [Rew.comp_app]; contradiction

def bvar (x : Fin n) : Operator L n := ⟨#x⟩

lemma operator_bvar (x : Fin k) (v : Fin k → Semiterm L ξ n) : (bvar x).operator v = v x := by
  simp [operator, bvar]

lemma bv_operator {k} (o : Operator L k) (v : Fin k → Semiterm L ξ (n + 1)) :
    (o.operator v).bv = .biUnion o.term.bv fun i ↦ (v i).bv  := by
  simp [operator]
  generalize o.term = s
  induction s <;> try simp [Rew.func, bv_func, Finset.biUnion_biUnion, *]
  case fvar => contradiction

lemma positive_operator_iff {k} {o : Operator L k} {v : Fin k → Semiterm L ξ (n + 1)} :
    (o.operator v).Positive ↔ ∀ i ∈ o.term.bv, (v i).Positive := by
  simp [Positive, bv_operator]
  exact ⟨fun h i hi x hx ↦ h x i hi hx, fun h x i hi hx ↦ h i hi x hx⟩

@[simp] lemma positive_const (c : Const L) : (c : Semiterm L ξ (n + 1)).Positive := by simp [const, positive_operator_iff]

-- f.operator ![ ... f.operator ![f.operator ![z, t 0], t 1], ... ,t (n-1)]
def foldr (f : Operator L 2) (z : Operator L k) : List (Operator L k) → Operator L k
  | []      => z
  | o :: os => f.comp ![foldr f z os, o]

@[simp] lemma foldr_nil (f : Operator L 2) (z : Operator L k) : f.foldr z [] = z := rfl

@[simp] lemma operator_foldr_cons (f : Operator L 2) (z : Operator L k) (o : Operator L k) (os : List (Operator L k))
  (v : Fin k → Semiterm L ξ n) :
    (f.foldr z (o :: os)).operator v = f.operator ![(f.foldr z os).operator v, o.operator v] := by
  simp [foldr, operator_comp, Matrix.fun_eq_vec₂]

def iterr (f : Operator L 2) (z : Const L) : (n : ℕ) → Operator L n
  | 0     => z
  | _ + 1 => f.foldr (bvar 0) (List.ofFn fun x => bvar x.succ)

@[simp] lemma iterr_zero (f : Operator L 2) (z : Const L) : f.iterr z 0 = z := rfl

informal_statement: For any two terms \( t \) and \( u \), and any operator \( o \) that takes two arguments, the value of applying \( o \) to \( t \) and \( u \) is the same as applying \( o \) directly to the values of \( t \) and \( u \) when evaluated in the context \( s \) with respect to expression \( e \) and environment \( \varepsilon \).
informal_proof:
By the definition of the operator's value evaluation (`val_operator`), the application of the operator \( o \) to the terms \( t \) and \( u \) respects the evaluation context. The `simp` tactic simplifies the expression, confirming that the value of \( o(t, u) \) in the given context \( s \), \( e \), and \( \varepsilon \) is equivalent to applying \( o \) directly to the evaluated values of \( t \) and \( u \).

Therefore, the equality \( \text{val}(s, e, \varepsilon)[o(\![t, u\]),] = o(\text{val}(s, e, \varepsilon)[t\], \text{val}(s, e, \varepsilon)[u\]) \) holds by the properties of the `val_operator` function and the simplification process.

import Foundation.FirstOrder.Basic.Semantics.Semantics
import Foundation.Vorspiel.NotationClass

namespace LO

namespace FirstOrder

variable {L : Language}

namespace Semiterm

structure Operator (L : Language) (n : ℕ) where
  term : Semiterm L Empty n

abbrev Const (L : Language.{u}) := Operator L 0

def fn {k} (f : L.Func k) : Operator L k := ⟨Semiterm.func f (#·)⟩

namespace Operator

def equiv : Operator L n ≃ Semiterm L Empty n where
  toFun := Operator.term
  invFun := Operator.mk
  left_inv := by intro _; simp
  right_inv := by intro _; simp

def operator {arity : ℕ} (o : Operator L arity) (v : Fin arity → Semiterm L ξ n) : Semiterm L ξ n :=
  Rew.substs v (Rew.emb o.term)

@[coe] abbrev const (c : Const L) : Semiterm L ξ n := c.operator ![]

instance : Coe (Const L) (Semiterm L ξ n) := ⟨Operator.const⟩

def comp (o : Operator L k) (w : Fin k → Operator L l) : Operator L l :=
  ⟨o.operator (fun x => (w x).term)⟩

@[simp] lemma operator_comp (o : Operator L k) (w : Fin k → Operator L l) (v : Fin l → Semiterm L ξ n) :
  (o.comp w).operator v = o.operator (fun x => (w x).operator v) := by
    simp [operator, comp, ←Rew.comp_app]; congr 1
    ext <;> simp [Rew.comp_app]; contradiction

def bvar (x : Fin n) : Operator L n := ⟨#x⟩

lemma operator_bvar (x : Fin k) (v : Fin k → Semiterm L ξ n) : (bvar x).operator v = v x := by
  simp [operator, bvar]

lemma bv_operator {k} (o : Operator L k) (v : Fin k → Semiterm L ξ (n + 1)) :
    (o.operator v).bv = .biUnion o.term.bv fun i ↦ (v i).bv  := by
  simp [operator]
  generalize o.term = s

informal_statement: For any operator `o` of type `Operator L 1`, the value of applying `o` to a value `s` with some context `ε` at index `![t]` is the same as first applying `o` to `s` and then to the indexed value `![t]`.
informal_proof: By applying the operator `o` to the value `s` at index `![t]` directly is equivalent to first applying `o` to `s` and then applying `o` to the specific component `![t]` of `s`. content_full:
import Foundation.FirstOrder.Basic.Semantics.Semantics
import Foundation.Vorspiel.NotationClass

namespace LO

namespace FirstOrder

variable {L : Language}

namespace Semiterm

structure Operator (L : Language) (n : ℕ) where
  term : Semiterm L Empty n

abbrev Const (L : Language.{u}) := Operator L 0

def fn {k} (f : L.Func k) : Operator L k := ⟨Semiterm.func f (#·)⟩

namespace Operator

def equiv : Operator L n ≃ Semiterm L Empty n where
  toFun := Operator.term
  invFun := Operator.mk
  left_inv := by intro _; simp
  right_inv := by intro _; simp

def operator {arity : ℕ} (o : Operator L arity) (v : Fin arity → Semiterm L ξ n) : Semiterm L ξ n :=
  Rew.substs v (Rew.emb o.term)

@[coe] abbrev const (c : Const L) : Semiterm L ξ n := c.operator ![]

instance : Coe (Const L) (Semiterm L ξ n) := ⟨Operator.const⟩

def comp (o : Operator L k) (w : Fin k → Operator L l) : Operator L l :=
  ⟨o.operator (fun x => (w x).term)⟩

@[simp] lemma operator_comp (o : Operator L k) (w : Fin k → Operator L l) (v : Fin l → Semiterm L ξ n) :
  (o.comp w).operator v = o.operator (fun x => (w x).operator v) := by
    simp [operator, comp, ←Rew.comp_app]; congr 1
    ext <;> simp [Rew.comp_app]; contradiction

def bvar (x : Fin n) : Operator L n := ⟨#x⟩

lemma operator_bvar (x : Fin k) (v : Fin k → Semiterm L ξ n) : (bvar x).operator v = v x := by
  simp [operator, bvar]

lemma bv_operator {k} (o : Operator L k) (v : Fin k → Semiterm L ξ (n + 1)) :
    (o.operator v).bv = .biUnion o.term.bv fun i ↦ (v i).bv  := by
  simp [operator]
  generalize o.term = s
  induction s <;> try simp [Rew.func, bv_func, Finset.biUnion_biUnion, *]
  case fvar => contradiction

lemma positive_operator_iff {k} {o : Operator L k} {v : Fin k → Semiterm L ξ (n + 1)} :
    (o.operator v).Positive ↔ ∀ i ∈ o.term.bv, (v i).Positive := by
  simp [Positive, bv_operator]
  exact ⟨fun h i hi x hx ↦ h x i hi hx, fun h x i hi hx ↦ h i hi x hx⟩

@[simp] lemma positive_const (c : Const L) : (c : Semiterm L ξ (n + 1)).Positive := by simp [const, positive_operator_iff]

-- f.operator ![ ... f.operator ![f.operator ![z, t 0], t 1], ... ,t (n-1)]
def foldr (f : Operator L 2) (z : Operator L k) : List (Operator L k) → Operator L k
  | []      => z
  | o :: os => f.comp ![foldr f z os, o]

@[simp] lemma foldr_nil (f : Operator L 2) (z : Operator L k) : f.foldr z [] = z := rfl

@[simp] lemma operator_foldr_cons (f : Operator L 2) (z : Operator L k) (o : Operator L k) (os : List (Operator L k))
  (v : Fin k → Semiterm L ξ n) :
    (f.foldr z (o :: os)).operator v = f.operator ![(f.foldr z os).operator v, o.operator v] := by
  simp [foldr, operator_comp, Matrix.fun_eq_vec₂]

def iterr (f : Operator L 2) (z : Const L) : (n : ℕ) → Operator L n
  | 0     => z
  | _ + 1 => f.foldr (bvar 0) (List.ofFn fun x => bvar x.succ)

@[simp] lemma iterr_zero (f : Operator L 2) (z : Const L) : f.iterr z 0 = z := rfl

def val (s : Structure L M) (e : Fin n → M) (ε : ξ → M) : Semiterm L ξ n → M
  | #x       => e x
  | &x       => ε x
  | func f v => s.func f (fun i => (v i).val s e ε)

rag.name: LO.FirstOrder.Semiterm.val_rew
rag.content:
lemma val_rew (ω : Rew L μ₁ n₁ μ₂ n₂) (t : Semiterm L μ₁ n₁) :
    (ω t).val s e₂ ε₂ = t.val s (val s e₂ ε₂ ∘ ω ∘ bvar) (val s e₂ ε₂ ∘ ω ∘ fvar) :=
  by induction t <;> simp [*, Rew.func, val_func]

rag.name: LO.FirstOrder.Semiformula.eval_toS
rag.content:
@[simp] lemma eval_toS {e : Fin n → M} {ε} (φ : Formula L (Fin n)) :
    Eval s e ε (@Rew.toS L n ▹ φ) ↔ Eval s ![] e φ := by
  simp [Rew.toS, eval_rew, Function.comp_def, Matrix.empty_eq]

rag.name: LO.FirstOrder.Semiformula.eval_rel₀
rag.content:
@[simp] lemma eval_rel₀ {r : L.Rel 0} :
    Eval s e ε (rel r ![]) ↔ s.rel r ![] := by simp [eval_rel, Matrix.empty_eq]

rag.name: Primrec.list_findIdx₁
rag.content:
theorem list_findIdx₁ {p : α → β → Bool} (hp : Primrec₂ p) :
    ∀ l : List β, Primrec fun a => l.findIdx (p a)
| [] => const 0
| a :: l => (cond (hp.comp .id (const a)) (const 0) (succ.comp (list_findIdx₁ hp l))).of_eq fun n =>
  by simp [List.findIdx_cons]

rag.name: LO.FirstOrder.Semiformula.Evalf
rag.content: abbrev Evalf (s : Structure L M) (ε : ξ → M) : Formula L ξ →ˡᶜ Prop := Eval s ![] ε

rag.name: LO.FirstOrder.Semiformula.eval_rel₂
rag.content:
@[simp] lemma eval_rel₂ {r : L.Rel 2} (t₁ t₂ : Semiterm L ξ n) :
    Eval s e ε (rel r ![t₁, t₂]) ↔ s.rel r ![t₁.val s e ε, t₂.val s e ε] := by
  simp [eval_rel]; apply of_eq; congr
  funext i; cases' i using Fin.cases with i <;> simp

informal_statement: The operator `o` from the class `Const L` is defined such that its value applied to an empty list is equal to `o.val`. This provides a foundational case for evaluating operators, particularly in contexts where operations may be applied to sequences or lists, possibly as an initial condition or base case in a larger proof or computation.
informal_proof: By invoking the simplifier tactic, we reduce the expression `val s e ε (o.operator v)` to `o.val ![]`, establishing that the operator `o` initialized with `v` evaluates to `o.val` when applied to an empty list. This simplification likely serves as a base case for further evaluations or proofs involving the operator `o` within the 'Const L' framework.

content_full:
import Foundation.FirstOrder.Basic.Semantics.Semantics
import Foundation.Vorspiel.NotationClass

namespace LO

namespace FirstOrder

variable {L : Language}

namespace Semiterm

structure Operator (L : Language) (n : ℕ) where
  term : Semiterm L Empty n

abbrev Const (L : Language.{u}) := Operator L 0

def fn {k} (f : L.Func k) : Operator L k := ⟨Semiterm.func f (#·)⟩

namespace Operator

def equiv : Operator L n ≃ Semiterm L Empty n where
  toFun := Operator.term
  invFun := Operator.mk
  left_inv := by intro _; simp
  right_inv := by intro _; simp

def operator {arity : ℕ} (o : Operator L arity) (v : Fin arity → Semiterm L ξ n) : Semiterm L ξ n :=
  Rew.substs v (Rew.emb o.term)

@[coe] abbrev const (c : Const L) : Semiterm L ξ n := c.operator ![]

instance : Coe (Const L) (Semiterm L ξ n) := ⟨Operator.const⟩

def comp (o : Operator L k) (w : Fin k → Operator L l) : Operator L l :=
  ⟨o.operator (fun x => (w x).term)⟩

@[simp] lemma operator_comp (o : Operator L k) (w : Fin k → Operator L l) (v : Fin l → Semiterm L ξ n) :
  (o.comp w).operator v = o.operator (fun x => (w x).operator v) := by
    simp [operator, comp, ←Rew.comp_app]; congr 1
    ext <;> simp [Rew.comp_app]; contradiction

def bvar (x : Fin n) : Operator L n := ⟨#x⟩

lemma operator_bvar (x : Fin k) (v : Fin k → Semiterm L ξ n) : (bvar x).operator v = v x := by
  simp [operator, bvar]

lemma bv_operator {k} (o : Operator L k) (v : Fin k → Semiterm L ξ (n + 1)) :
    (o.operator v).bv = .biUnion o.term.bv fun i ↦ (v i).bv  := by
  simp [operator]
  generalize o.term = s
  induction s <;> try simp [Rew.func, bv_func, Finset.biUnion_biUnion, *]
  case fvar => contradiction

lemma positive_operator_iff {k} {o : Operator L k} {v : Fin k → Semiterm L ξ (n + 1)} :
    (o.operator v).Positive ↔ ∀ i ∈ o.term.bv, (v i).Positive := by
  simp [Positive, bv_operator]
  exact ⟨fun h i hi x hx ↦ h x i hi hx, fun h x i hi hx ↦ h i hi x hx⟩

@[simp] lemma positive_const (c : Const L) : (c : Semiterm L ξ (n + 1)).Positive := by simp [const, positive_operator_iff]

-- f.operator ![ ... f.operator ![f.operator ![z, t 0], t 1], ... ,t (n-1)]
def foldr (f : Operator L 2) (z : Operator L k) : List (Operator L k) → Operator L k
  | []      => z
  | o :: os => f.comp ![foldr f z os, o]

@[simp] lemma foldr_nil (f : Operator L 2) (z : Operator L k) : f.foldr z [] = z := rfl

@[simp] lemma operator_foldr_cons (f : Operator L 2) (z : Operator L k) (o : Operator L k) (os : List (Operator L k))
  (v : Fin k → Semiterm L ξ n) :
    (f.foldr z (o :: os)).operator v = f.operator ![(f.foldr z os).operator v, o.operator v] := by
  simp [foldr, operator_comp, Matrix.fun_eq_vec₂]

def iterr (f : Operator L 2) (z : Const L) : (n : ℕ) → Operator L n
  | 0     => z
  | _ + 1 => f.foldr (bvar 0) (List.ofFn fun x => bvar x.succ)

@[simp] lemma iterr_zero (f : Operator L 2) (z : Const L) : f.iterr z 0 = z := rfl

informal_statement: The value of the constant operator `o.const` is equal to the value of `o`.
informal_proof: By applying the simplification lemmas `Operator.const`, `val_operator`, and `Matrix.empty_eq`, we directly obtain the desired equality: `val s e ε o.const = o.val ![]`. This follows because `o.const` is defined to be a constant value associated with `o`, and the simplification steps reduce the expression to its base value. Therefore, the equality holds as both sides represent the same value.

content_full:
import Foundation.FirstOrder.Basic.Semantics.Semantics
import Foundation.Vorspiel.NotationClass

namespace LO

namespace FirstOrder

variable {L : Language}

namespace Semiterm

structure Operator (L : Language) (n : ℕ) where
  term : Semiterm L Empty n

abbrev Const (L : Language.{u}) := Operator L 0

def fn {k} (f : L.Func k) : Operator L k := ⟨Semiterm.func f (#·)⟩

namespace Operator

def equiv : Operator L n ≃ Semiterm L Empty n where
  toFun := Operator.term
  invFun := Operator.mk
  left_inv := by intro _; simp
  right_inv := by intro _; simp

def operator {arity : ℕ} (o : Operator L arity) (v : Fin arity → Semiterm L ξ n) : Semiterm L ξ n :=
  Rew.substs v (Rew.emb o.term)

@[coe] abbrev const (c : Const L) : Semiterm L ξ n := c.operator ![]

instance : Coe (Const L) (Semiterm L ξ n) := ⟨Operator.const⟩

def comp (o : Operator L k) (w : Fin k → Operator L l) : Operator L l :=
  ⟨o.operator (fun x => (w x).term)⟩

@[simp] lemma operator_comp (o : Operator L k) (w : Fin k → Operator L l) (v : Fin l → Semiterm L ξ n) :
  (o.comp w).operator v = o.operator (fun x => (w x).operator v) := by
    simp [operator, comp, ←Rew.comp_app]; congr 1
    ext <;> simp [Rew.comp_app]; contradiction

def bvar (x : Fin n) : Operator L n := ⟨#x⟩

lemma operator_bvar (x : Fin k) (v : Fin k → Semiterm L ξ n) : (bvar x).operator v = v x := by
  simp [operator, bvar]

lemma bv_operator {k} (o : Operator L k) (v : Fin k → Semiterm L ξ (n + 1)) :
    (o.operator v).bv = .biUnion o.term.bv fun i ↦ (v i).bv  := by
  simp [operator]
  generalize o.term = s
  induction s <;> try simp [Rew.func, bv_func, Finset.biUnion_biUnion, *]
  case fvar => contradiction

lemma positive_operator_iff {k} {o : Operator L k} {v : Fin k → Semiterm L ξ (n + 1)} :
    (o.operator v).Positive ↔ ∀ i ∈ o.term.bv, (v i).Positive := by
  simp [Positive, bv_operator]
  exact ⟨fun h i hi x hx ↦ h x i hi hx, fun h x i hi hx ↦ h i hi x hx⟩

@[simp] lemma positive_const (c : Const L) : (c : Semiterm L ξ (n + 1)).Positive := by simp [const, positive_operator_iff]

-- f.operator ![ ... f.operator ![f.operator ![z, t 0], t 1], ... ,t (n-1)]
def foldr (f : Operator L 2) (z : Operator L k) : List (Operator L k) → Operator L k
  | []      => z
  | o :: os => f.comp ![foldr f z os, o]

@[simp] lemma foldr_nil (f : Operator L 2) (z : Operator L k) : f.foldr z [] = z := rfl

@[simp] lemma operator_foldr_cons (f : Operator L 2) (z : Operator L k) (o : Operator L k) (os : List (Operator L k))
  (v : Fin k → Semiterm L ξ n) :
    (f.foldr z (o :: os)).operator v = f.operator ![(f.foldr z os).operator v, o.operator v] := by
  simp [foldr, operator_comp, Matrix.fun_eq_vec₂]

def iterr (f : Operator L 2) (z : Const L) : (n : ℕ) → Operator L n
  | 0     => z
  | _ + 1 => f.foldr (bvar 0) (List.ofFn fun x => bvar x.succ)

@[simp] lemma iterr_zero (f : Operator L 2) (z : Const L) : f.iterr z 0 = z := rfl

rag.content:
lemma val_func {k} (f : L.Func k) (v) :
    val s e ε (func f v) = s.func f (fun i => (v i).val s e ε) := rfl

rag.name: LO.FirstOrder.Semiterm.val_embSubsts
rag.content:
lemma val_embSubsts (w : Fin k → Semiterm L ξ n) (t : Semiterm L Empty k) :
    (Rew.embSubsts w t).val s e ε = t.valb s (fun x ↦ (w x).val s e ε) := by
  simp [val_rew, Empty.eq_elim]; congr

rag.name: LO.FirstOrder.Semiterm.val_func₁
rag.content:

    val s e ε (func f ![t]) = s.func f ![t.val s e ε] :=
  by simp [val_func]; congr; funext i; cases' i using Fin.cases with i <;> simp

rag.name: LO.FirstOrder.Semiterm.val_bvar
rag.content: @[simp] lemma val_bvar (x) : val s e ε (#x : Semiterm L ξ n) = e x := rfl

rag.name: LO.FirstOrder.Semiterm.val_rewrite
rag.content:
lemma val_rewrite (f : μ₁ → Semiterm L μ₂ n) (t : Semiterm L μ₁ n) :
    (Rew.rewrite f t).val s e ε₂ = t.val s e (fun x => (f x).val s e ε₂) :=
  by simp [val_rew]; congr

rag.name: LO.FirstOrder.Semiterm.valm
rag.content: abbrev valm (M : Type w) [s : Structure L M] {n} (e : Fin n → M) (ε : ξ → M) : Semiterm L ξ n → M := val s e ε

rag.name: LO.FirstOrder.Semiterm.val_rew
rag.content:
lemma val_rew (ω : Rew L μ₁ n₁ μ₂ n₂) (t : Semiterm L μ₁ n₁) :
    (ω t).val s e₂ ε₂ = t.val s (val s e₂ ε₂ ∘ ω ∘ bvar) (val s e₂ ε₂ ∘ ω ∘ fvar) :=
  by induction t <;> simp [*, Rew.func, val_func]

rag.name: LO.FirstOrder.Semiterm.val
rag.content:
def val (s : Structure L M) (e : Fin n → M) (ε : ξ → M) : Semiterm L ξ n → M
  | #x       => e x
  | &x       => ε x
  | func f v => s.func f (fun i => (v i).val s e ε)

rag.name: LO.FirstOrder.Semiterm.val_rewriteMap
rag.content:
lemma val_rewriteMap (f : μ₁ → μ₂) (t : Semiterm L μ₁ n) :
    (Rew.rewriteMap f t).val s e ε₂ = t.val s e (fun x => ε₂ (f x)) :=
  by simp [val_rew]; congr

rag.name: LO.FirstOrder.Semiterm.val_substs
rag.content:
lemma val_substs (w : Fin n₁ → Semiterm L ξ n₂) (t : Semiterm L ξ n₁) :
    (Rew.substs w t).val s e₂ ε = t.val s (fun x => (w x).val s e₂ ε) ε :=
  by simp [val_rew]; congr

informal_statement: For any context or type $k$, and any operator $op$ of type $L(k)$ and any value $v$ of type $val\ s\ e\ ε\ v$, the result of applying $op$ to $v$ is equivalent to applying $op.val$ to the function that extracts the value of $v$ in the context $s$, environment $e$, and epsilon $ε$.
informal_proof:
We start with the given operator $op$ of type $L(k)$ and any value $v$ of type $val\ s\ e\ ε\ v$. By applying the simplification rule that handles the operator and value extraction (as given in `val_substs`), we reduce the expression to an equality that remains true. 

Next, we use the congruence property, which allows us to assert that if two functions are structurally identical, they are equal when applied to the same inputs. This ensures that the transformed expression preserves the original meaning and equality condition.

Finally, by applying function extensionality, we confirm that the two sides of the equation are equal for all possible inputs within the domain defined by $s$, $e$, and $ε$. This completes the proof that the original statement holds true under the given conditions.

content_full:
import Foundation.FirstOrder.Basic.Semantics.Semantics
import Foundation.Vorspiel.NotationClass

namespace LO

namespace FirstOrder

variable {L : Language}

namespace Semiterm

structure Operator (L : Language) (n : ℕ) where
  term : Semiterm L Empty n

abbrev Const (L : Language.{u}) := Operator L 0

def fn {k} (f : L.Func k) : Operator L k := ⟨Semiterm.func f (#·)⟩

namespace Operator

def equiv : Operator L n ≃ Semiterm L Empty n where
  toFun := Operator.term
  invFun := Operator.mk
  left_inv := by intro _; simp
  right_inv := by intro _; simp

def operator {arity : ℕ} (o : Operator L arity) (v : Fin arity → Semiterm L ξ n) : Semiterm L ξ n :=
  Rew.substs v (Rew.emb o.term)

@[coe] abbrev const (c : Const L) : Semiterm L ξ n := c.operator ![]

instance : Coe (Const L) (Semiterm L ξ n) := ⟨Operator.const⟩

def comp (o : Operator L k) (w : Fin k → Operator L l) : Operator L l :=
  ⟨o.operator (fun x => (w x).term)⟩

@[simp] lemma operator_comp (o : Operator L k) (w : Fin k → Operator L l) (v : Fin l → Semiterm L ξ n) :
  (o.comp w).operator v = o.operator (fun x => (w x).operator v) := by
    simp [operator, comp, ←Rew.comp_app]; congr 1
    ext <;> simp [Rew.comp_app]; contradiction

def bvar (x : Fin n) : Operator L n := ⟨#x⟩

lemma operator_bvar (x : Fin k) (v : Fin k → Semiterm L ξ n) : (bvar x).operator v = v x := by
  simp [operator, bvar]

lemma bv_operator {k} (o : Operator L k) (v : Fin k → Semiterm L ξ (n + 1)) :
    (o.operator v).bv = .biUnion o.term.bv fun i ↦ (v i).bv  := by
  simp [operator]
  generalize o.term = s
  induction s <;> try simp [Rew.func, bv_func, Finset.biUnion_biUnion, *]
  case fvar => contradiction

lemma positive_operator_iff {k} {o : Operator L k} {v : Fin k → Semiterm L ξ (n + 1)} :
    (o.operator v).Positive ↔ ∀ i ∈ o.term.bv, (v i).Positive := by
  simp [Positive, bv_operator]
  exact ⟨fun h i hi x hx ↦ h x i hi hx, fun h x i hi hx ↦ h i hi x hx⟩

@[simp] lemma positive_const (c : Const L) : (c : Semiterm L ξ (n + 1)).Positive := by simp [const, positive_operator_iff]

-- f.operator ![ ... f.operator ![f.operator ![z, t 0], t 1], ... ,t (n-1)]
def foldr (f : Operator L 2) (z : Operator L k) : List (Operator L k) → Operator L k
  | []      => z
  | o :: os => f.comp ![foldr f z os, o]

@[simp] lemma foldr_nil (f : Operator L 2) (z : Operator L k) : f.foldr z [] = z := rfl

@[simp] lemma operator_foldr_cons (f : Operator L 2) (z : Operator L k) (o : Operator L k) (os : List (Operator L k))
  (v : Fin k → Semiterm L ξ n) :
    (f.foldr z (o :: os)).operator v = f.operator ![(f.foldr z os).operator v, o.operator v] := by
  simp [foldr, operator_comp, Matrix.fun_eq_vec₂]

def iterr (f : Operator L 2) (z : Const L) : (n : ℕ) → Operator L n
  | 0     => z
  | _ + 1 => f.foldr (bvar 0) (List.ofFn fun x => bvar x.succ)

@[simp] lemma iterr_zero (f : Operator L 2) (z : Const L) : f.iterr z 0 = z := rfl

content_full:
import Foundation.FirstOrder.Basic.Semantics.Semantics
import Foundation.Vorspiel.NotationClass

namespace LO

namespace FirstOrder

variable {L : Language}

namespace Semiterm

structure Operator (L : Language) (n : ℕ) where
  term : Semiterm L Empty n

abbrev Const (L : Language.{u}) := Operator L 0

def fn {k} (f : L.Func k) : Operator L k := ⟨Semiterm.func f (#·)⟩

namespace Operator

def equiv : Operator L n ≃ Semiterm L Empty n where
  toFun := Operator.term
  invFun := Operator.mk
  left_inv := by intro _; simp
  right_inv := by intro _; simp

def operator {arity : ℕ} (o : Operator L arity) (v : Fin arity → Semiterm L ξ n) : Semiterm L ξ n :=
  Rew.substs v (Rew.emb o.term)

@[coe] abbrev const (c : Const L) : Semiterm L ξ n := c.operator ![]

instance : Coe (Const L) (Semiterm L ξ n) := ⟨Operator.const⟩

def comp (o : Operator L k) (w : Fin k → Operator L l) : Operator L l :=
  ⟨o.operator (fun x => (w x).term)⟩

@[simp] lemma operator_comp (o : Operator L k) (w : Fin k → Operator L l) (v : Fin l → Semiterm L ξ n) :
  (o.comp w).operator v = o.operator (fun x => (w x).operator v) := by
    simp [operator, comp, ←Rew.comp_app]; congr 1
    ext <;> simp [Rew.comp_app]; contradiction

def bvar (x : Fin n) : Operator L n := ⟨#x⟩

lemma operator_bvar (x : Fin k) (v : Fin k → Semiterm L ξ n) : (bvar x).operator v = v x := by
  simp [operator, bvar]

lemma bv_operator {k} (o : Operator L k) (v : Fin k → Semiterm L ξ (n + 1)) :
    (o.operator v).bv = .biUnion o.term.bv fun i ↦ (v i).bv  := by
  simp [operator]
  generalize o.term = s
  induction s <;> try simp [Rew.func, bv_func, Finset.biUnion_biUnion, *]
  case fvar => contradiction

lemma positive_operator_iff {k} {o : Operator L k} {v : Fin k → Semiterm L ξ (n + 1)} :
    (o.operator v).Positive ↔ ∀ i ∈ o.term.bv, (v i).Positive := by
  simp [Positive, bv_operator]
  exact ⟨fun h i hi x hx ↦ h x i hi hx, fun h x i hi hx ↦ h i hi x hx⟩

@[simp] lemma positive_const (c : Const L) : (c : Semiterm L ξ (n + 1)).Positive := by simp [const, positive_operator_iff]

-- f.operator ![ ... f.operator ![f.operator ![z, t 0], t 1], ... ,t (n-1)]
def foldr (f : Operator L 2) (z : Operator L k) : List (Operator L k) → Operator L k
  | []      => z
  | o :: os => f.comp ![foldr f z os, o]

@[simp] lemma foldr_nil (f : Operator L 2) (z : Operator L k) : f.foldr z [] = z := rfl

@[simp] lemma operator_foldr_cons (f : Operator L 2) (z : Operator L k) (o : Operator L k) (os : List (Operator L k))
  (v : Fin k → Semiterm L ξ n) :
    (f.foldr z (o :: os)).operator v = f.operator ![(f.foldr z os).operator v, o.operator v] := by
  simp [foldr, operator_comp, Matrix.fun_eq_vec₂]

def iterr (f : Operator L 2) (z : Const L) : (n : ℕ) → Operator L n
  | 0     => z
  | _ + 1 => f.foldr (bvar 0) (List.ofFn fun x => bvar x.succ)

@[simp] lemma iterr_zero (f : Operator L 2) (z : Const L) : f.iterr z 0 = z := rfl

rag.content:
def complexity {n : ℕ} : Semiformula L ξ n → ℕ
| ⊤        => 0
| ⊥        => 0
| rel _ _  => 0
| nrel _ _ => 0
| φ ⋏ ψ    => max φ.complexity ψ.complexity + 1
| φ ⋎ ψ    => max φ.complexity ψ.complexity + 1
| ∀' φ     => φ.complexity + 1
| ∃' φ     => φ.complexity + 1

rag.name: LO.FirstOrder.Semiformula.complexity_and
rag.content: @[simp] lemma complexity_and (φ ψ : Semiformula L ξ n) : complexity (φ ⋏ ψ) = max φ.complexity ψ.complexity + 1 := rfl

rag.content: @[simp] lemma complexity_and' (φ ψ : Semiformula L ξ n) : complexity (and φ ψ) = max φ.complexity ψ.complexity + 1 := rfl

rag.name: LO.FirstOrder.Semiterm.complexity
rag.content:
def complexity : Semiterm L ξ n → ℕ
  | #_       => 0
  | &_       => 0
  | func _ v => Finset.sup Finset.univ (fun i ↦ complexity (v i)) + 1

rag.name: LO.FirstOrder.Semiterm.complexity_fvar
rag.content: @[simp] lemma complexity_fvar (x : ξ) : (&x : Semiterm L ξ n).complexity = 0 := rfl

rag.name: LO.FirstOrder.Semiformula.complexity_or'
rag.content: @[simp] lemma complexity_or' (φ ψ : Semiformula L ξ n) : complexity (or φ ψ) = max φ.complexity ψ.complexity + 1 := rfl

rag.name: LO.FirstOrder.Semiformula.complexity_rel
rag.content: @[simp] lemma complexity_rel {k} (r : L.Rel k) (v : Fin k → Semiterm L ξ n) : complexity (rel r v) = 0 := rfl

rag.name: LO.FirstOrder.Semiformula.complexity_all'
rag.content: @[simp] lemma complexity_all' (φ : Semiformula L ξ (n + 1)) : complexity (all φ) = φ.complexity + 1 := rfl

rag.name: LO.FirstOrder.Semiformula.complexity_ex
rag.content: @[simp] lemma complexity_ex (φ : Semiformula L ξ (n + 1)) : complexity (∃' φ) = φ.complexity + 1 := rfl

rag.name: LO.FirstOrder.Semiformula.complexity_top
rag.content: @[simp] lemma complexity_top : complexity (⊤ : Semiformula L ξ n) = 0 := rfl

informal_statement: For any two semiterms \( t \) and \( u \) in \( \text{Semiterm}(L, \xi, n) \), the complexity of their product is equal to the maximum of their individual complexities plus one.
informal_proof:
To prove this statement, we begin by understanding the definitions and properties of semiterms and the complexity function \( \text{complexity\_func} \).

1. **Definitions**:
   - **Semiterm**: A semiterm is a foundational element used in the construction of more complex expressions within a formal system. It can be thought of as a node in an expression tree, representing a basic unit of computation or combination.
   - **Complexity**: The function \( \text{complexity\_func} \) assigns a numerical value to each semiterm, reflecting the complexity or "size" of the term. This can represent the number of operations, resources, or logical steps required to compute the term.

2. **Base Case**:
   - For the simplest semiterms (e.g., constants or variables), the complexity is defined to be 0. This serves as the foundation for building the complexity of more complex terms.

3. **Recursive Construction**:
   - When building more complex semiterms by combining existing ones (e.g., applying operators), the complexity of the new term is determined by its components.
   - Specifically, when two semiterms \( t \) and \( u \) are multiplied, the resulting term's complexity is given by \( \max(\text{complexity\_func}(t), \text{complexity\_func}(u)) + 1 \).
   - This rule reflects the idea that multiplying two terms often introduces an extra layer of complexity, accounting for the multiplication operation itself.

4. **Proof by Induction**:
   - **Inductive Step**: Assume that for any two semiterms \( t \) and \( u \) with complexities \( c_t \) and \( c_u \) respectively, multiplying them results in a term with complexity \( \max(c_t, c_u) + 1 \).
   - Consider the operation of multiplication applied to \( t \) and \( u \). By definition, this operation combines \( t \) and \( u \) and introduces one additional operation step.
   - Thus, the complexity of the resulting term naturally becomes \( \max(\text{complexity\_func}(t), \text{complexity\_func}(u)) + 1 \).

5. **Conclusion**:
   - Therefore, for all semiterms \( t \) and \( u \) in \( \text{Semiterm}(L, \xi, n) \), the complexity of their product \( t \cdot u \) is equal to the maximum of their individual complexities plus one.

content_full:
import Foundation.FirstOrder.Basic.Semantics.Semantics
import Foundation.Vorspiel.NotationClass

namespace LO

namespace FirstOrder

variable {L : Language}

namespace Semiterm

structure Operator (L : Language) (n : ℕ) where
  term : Semiterm L Empty n

abbrev Const (L : Language.{u}) := Operator L 0

def fn {k} (f : L.Func k) : Operator L k := ⟨Semiterm.func f (#·)⟩

namespace Operator

def equiv : Operator L n ≃ Semiterm L Empty n where
  toFun := Operator.term
  invFun := Operator.mk
  left_inv := by intro _; simp
  right_inv := by intro _; simp

def operator {arity : ℕ} (o : Operator L arity) (v : Fin arity → Semiterm L ξ n) : Semiterm L ξ n :=
  Rew.substs v (Rew.emb o.term)

@[coe] abbrev const (c : Const L) : Semiterm L ξ n := c.operator ![]

instance : Coe (Const L) (Semiterm L ξ n) := ⟨Operator.const⟩

def comp (o : Operator L k) (w : Fin k → Operator L l) : Operator L l :=
  ⟨o.operator (fun x => (w x).term)⟩

@[simp] lemma operator_comp (o : Operator L k) (w : Fin k → Operator L l) (v : Fin l → Semiterm L ξ n) :
  (o.comp w).operator v = o.operator (fun x => (w x).operator v) := by
    simp [operator, comp, ←Rew.comp_app]; congr 1
    ext <;> simp [Rew.comp_app]; contradiction

def bvar (x : Fin n) : Operator L n := ⟨#x⟩

lemma operator_bvar (x : Fin k) (v : Fin k → Semiterm L ξ n) : (bvar x).operator v = v x := by
  simp [operator, bvar]

lemma bv_operator {k} (o : Operator L k) (v : Fin k → Semiterm L ξ (n + 1)) :
    (o.operator v).bv = .biUnion o.term.bv fun i ↦ (v i).bv  := by
  simp [operator]
  generalize o.term = s
  induction s <;> try simp [Rew.func, bv_func, Finset.biUnion_biUnion, *]
  case fvar => contradiction

lemma positive_operator_iff {k} {o : Operator L k} {v : Fin k → Semiterm L ξ (n + 1)} :
    (o.operator v).Positive ↔ ∀ i ∈ o.term.bv, (v i).Positive := by
  simp [Positive, bv_operator]
  exact ⟨fun h i hi x hx ↦ h x i hi hx, fun h x i hi hx ↦ h i hi x hx⟩

@[simp] lemma positive_const (c : Const L) : (c : Semiterm L ξ (n + 1)).Positive := by simp [const, positive_operator_iff]

-- f.operator ![ ... f.operator ![f.operator ![z, t 0], t 1], ... ,t (n-1)]
def foldr (f : Operator L 2) (z : Operator L k) : List (Operator L k) → Operator L k
  | []      => z
  | o :: os => f.comp ![foldr f z os, o]

@[simp] lemma foldr_nil (f : Operator L 2) (z : Operator L k) : f.foldr z [] = z := rfl

@[simp] lemma operator_foldr_cons (f : Operator L 2) (z : Operator L k) (o : Operator L k) (os : List (Operator L k))
  (v : Fin k → Semiterm L ξ n) :
    (f.foldr z (o :: os)).operator v = f.operator ![(f.foldr z os).operator v, o.operator v] := by
  simp [foldr, operator_comp, Matrix.fun_eq_vec₂]

def iterr (f : Operator L 2) (z : Const L) : (n : ℕ) → Operator L n
  | 0     => z
  | _ + 1 => f.foldr (bvar 0) (List.ofFn fun x => bvar x.succ)

@[simp] lemma iterr_zero (f : Operator L 2) (z : Const L) : f.iterr z 0 = z := rfl

def complexity {n : ℕ} : Semiformula L ξ n → ℕ
| ⊤        => 0

| φ ⋎ ψ    => max φ.complexity ψ.complexity + 1

informal_statement: For any two semiterms \( t \) and \( u \), the complexity of their addition is equal to one greater than the maximum complexity among \( t \) and \( u \).
informal_proof:
Let \( t \) and \( u \) be arbitrary semiterms, and let \( + \) denote the addition operation. The complexity of the addition \( t + u \) is determined based on the complexities of \( t \) and \( u \).

1. **Simplification and Definitions**: 
   
   - We start by using the definition of the addition operator applied to semiterms \( t \) and \( u \).
   - According to the given definitions, the complexity of the addition operation \( t + u \) is defined as \( max(t.complexity, u.complexity) + 1 \).

2. **Calculation of Complexity**:
   
   - The expression \( max(t.complexity, u.complexity) + 1 \) directly defines the complexity of \( t + u \).
   - This means that if \( t \) has a complexity of \( n \) and \( u \) has a complexity of \( m \), then the complexity of \( t + u \) will be \( max(n, m) + 1 \).

3. **Conclusion**:
   
   - Therefore, for any two semiterms \( t \) and \( u \), the complexity of their addition \( t + u \) is always one more than the higher complexity between \( t \) and \( u \).
   - This aligns with the property of addition in terms of complexity as stated in the formal lemma.

Hence, we conclude that the complexity of adding two semiterms is as described, with each step logically following from the definitions and properties involved.

import Foundation.FirstOrder.Basic.Semantics.Semantics
import Foundation.Vorspiel.NotationClass

namespace LO

namespace FirstOrder

variable {L : Language}

namespace Semiterm

structure Operator (L : Language) (n : ℕ) where
  term : Semiterm L Empty n

abbrev Const (L : Language.{u}) := Operator L 0

def fn {k} (f : L.Func k) : Operator L k := ⟨Semiterm.func f (#·)⟩

namespace Operator

def equiv : Operator L n ≃ Semiterm L Empty n where
  toFun := Operator.term
  invFun := Operator.mk
  left_inv := by intro _; simp
  right_inv := by intro _; simp

def operator {arity : ℕ} (o : Operator L arity) (v : Fin arity → Semiterm L ξ n) : Semiterm L ξ n :=
  Rew.substs v (Rew.emb o.term)

@[coe] abbrev const (c : Const L) : Semiterm L ξ n := c.operator ![]

instance : Coe (Const L) (Semiterm L ξ n) := ⟨Operator.const⟩

def comp (o : Operator L k) (w : Fin k → Operator L l) : Operator L l :=
  ⟨o.operator (fun x => (w x).term)⟩

@[simp] lemma operator_comp (o : Operator L k) (w : Fin k → Operator L l) (v : Fin l → Semiterm L ξ n) :
  (o.comp w).operator v = o.operator (fun x => (w x).operator v) := by
    simp [operator, comp, ←Rew.comp_app]; congr 1
    ext <;> simp [Rew.comp_app]; contradiction

def bvar (x : Fin n) : Operator L n := ⟨#x⟩

lemma operator_bvar (x : Fin k) (v : Fin k → Semiterm L ξ n) : (bvar x).operator v = v x := by
  simp [operator, bvar]

lemma bv_operator {k} (o : Operator L k) (v : Fin k → Semiterm L ξ (n + 1)) :
    (o.operator v).bv = .biUnion o.term.bv fun i ↦ (v i).bv  := by
  simp [operator]
  generalize o.term = s
  induction s <;> try simp [Rew.func, bv_func, Finset.biUnion_biUnion, *]
  case fvar => contradiction

lemma positive_operator_iff {k} {o : Operator L k} {v : Fin k → Semiterm L ξ (n + 1)} :
    (o.operator v).Positive ↔ ∀ i ∈ o.term.bv, (v i).Positive := by
  simp [Positive, bv_operator]
  exact ⟨fun h i hi x hx ↦ h x i hi hx, fun h x i hi hx ↦ h i hi x hx⟩

@[simp] lemma positive_const (c : Const L) : (c : Semiterm L ξ (n + 1)).Positive := by simp [const, positive_operator_iff]

-- f.operator ![ ... f.operator ![f.operator ![z, t 0], t 1], ... ,t (n-1)]
def foldr (f : Operator L 2) (z : Operator L k) : List (Operator L k) → Operator L k
  | []      => z
  | o :: os => f.comp ![foldr f z os, o]

@[simp] lemma foldr_nil (f : Operator L 2) (z : Operator L k) : f.foldr z [] = z := rfl

@[simp] lemma operator_foldr_cons (f : Operator L 2) (z : Operator L k) (o : Operator L k) (os : List (Operator L k))
  (v : Fin k → Semiterm L ξ n) :
    (f.foldr z (o :: os)).operator v = f.operator ![(f.foldr z os).operator v, o.operator v] := by
  simp [foldr, operator_comp, Matrix.fun_eq_vec₂]

def iterr (f : Operator L 2) (z : Const L) : (n : ℕ) → Operator L n
  | 0     => z
  | _ + 1 => f.foldr (bvar 0) (List.ofFn fun x => bvar x.succ)

@[simp] lemma iterr_zero (f : Operator L 2) (z : Const L) : f.iterr z 0 = z := rfl

def complexity {n : ℕ} : Semiformula L ξ n → ℕ
| ⊤        => 0
| ⊥        => 0
| rel _ _  => 0
| nrel _ _ => 0
| φ ⋏ ψ    => max φ.complexity ψ.complexity + 1
| φ ⋎ ψ    => max φ.complexity ψ.complexity + 1
| ∀' φ     => φ.complexity + 1
| ∃' φ     => φ.complexity + 1

  | #_       => 0

  | func _ v => Finset.sup Finset.univ (fun i ↦ complexity (v i)) + 1

  induction φ using Semiformula.rec' generalizing n₂ <;> simp [*, rew_rel, rew_nrel]

import Foundation.FirstOrder.Basic.Semantics.Semantics
import Foundation.Vorspiel.NotationClass

namespace LO

namespace FirstOrder

variable {L : Language}

namespace Semiterm

structure Operator (L : Language) (n : ℕ) where
  term : Semiterm L Empty n

abbrev Const (L : Language.{u}) := Operator L 0

def fn {k} (f : L.Func k) : Operator L k := ⟨Semiterm.func f (#·)⟩

namespace Operator

def equiv : Operator L n ≃ Semiterm L Empty n where
  toFun := Operator.term
  invFun := Operator.mk
  left_inv := by intro _; simp
  right_inv := by intro _; simp

def operator {arity : ℕ} (o : Operator L arity) (v : Fin arity → Semiterm L ξ n) : Semiterm L ξ n :=
  Rew.substs v (Rew.emb o.term)

@[coe] abbrev const (c : Const L) : Semiterm L ξ n := c.operator ![]

instance : Coe (Const L) (Semiterm L ξ n) := ⟨Operator.const⟩

def comp (o : Operator L k) (w : Fin k → Operator L l) : Operator L l :=
  ⟨o.operator (fun x => (w x).term)⟩

@[simp] lemma operator_comp (o : Operator L k) (w : Fin k → Operator L l) (v : Fin l → Semiterm L ξ n) :
  (o.comp w).operator v = o.operator (fun x => (w x).operator v) := by
    simp [operator, comp, ←Rew.comp_app]; congr 1
    ext <;> simp [Rew.comp_app]; contradiction

def bvar (x : Fin n) : Operator L n := ⟨#x⟩

lemma operator_bvar (x : Fin k) (v : Fin k → Semiterm L ξ n) : (bvar x).operator v = v x := by
  simp [operator, bvar]

lemma bv_operator {k} (o : Operator L k) (v : Fin k → Semiterm L ξ (n + 1)) :
    (o.operator v).bv = .biUnion o.term.bv fun i ↦ (v i).bv  := by
  simp [operator]
  generalize o.term = s
  induction s <;> try simp [Rew.func, bv_func, Finset.biUnion_biUnion, *]
  case fvar => contradiction

lemma positive_operator_iff {k} {o : Operator L k} {v : Fin k → Semiterm L ξ (n + 1)} :
    (o.operator v).Positive ↔ ∀ i ∈ o.term.bv, (v i).Positive := by
  simp [Positive, bv_operator]
  exact ⟨fun h i hi x hx ↦ h x i hi hx, fun h x i hi hx ↦ h i hi x hx⟩

@[simp] lemma positive_const (c : Const L) : (c : Semiterm L ξ (n + 1)).Positive := by simp [const, positive_operator_iff]

-- f.operator ![ ... f.operator ![f.operator ![z, t 0], t 1], ... ,t (n-1)]
def foldr (f : Operator L 2) (z : Operator L k) : List (Operator L k) → Operator L k
  | []      => z
  | o :: os => f.comp ![foldr f z os, o]

@[simp] lemma foldr_nil (f : Operator L 2) (z : Operator L k) : f.foldr z [] = z := rfl

@[simp] lemma operator_foldr_cons (f : Operator L 2) (z : Operator L k) (o : Operator L k) (os : List (Operator L k))
  (v : Fin k → Semiterm L ξ n) :
    (f.foldr z (o :: os)).operator v = f.operator ![(f.foldr z os).operator v, o.operator v] := by
  simp [foldr, operator_comp, Matrix.fun_eq_vec₂]

def iterr (f : Operator L 2) (z : Const L) : (n : ℕ) → Operator L n
  | 0     => z
  | _ + 1 => f.foldr (bvar 0) (List.ofFn fun x => bvar x.succ)

@[simp] lemma iterr_zero (f : Operator L 2) (z : Const L) : f.iterr z 0 = z := rfl

def complexity {n : ℕ} : Semiformula L ξ n → ℕ
| ⊤        => 0
| ⊥        => 0
| rel _ _  => 0
| nrel _ _ => 0
| φ ⋏ ψ    => max φ.complexity ψ.complexity + 1
| φ ⋎ ψ    => max φ.complexity ψ.complexity + 1
| ∀' φ     => φ.complexity + 1
| ∃' φ     => φ.complexity + 1

import Foundation.FirstOrder.Basic.Semantics.Semantics
import Foundation.Vorspiel.NotationClass

namespace LO

namespace FirstOrder

variable {L : Language}

namespace Semiterm

structure Operator (L : Language) (n : ℕ) where
  term : Semiterm L Empty n

abbrev Const (L : Language.{u}) := Operator L 0

def fn {k} (f : L.Func k) : Operator L k := ⟨Semiterm.func f (#·)⟩

namespace Operator

def equiv : Operator L n ≃ Semiterm L Empty n where
  toFun := Operator.term
  invFun := Operator.mk
  left_inv := by intro _; simp
  right_inv := by intro _; simp

def operator {arity : ℕ} (o : Operator L arity) (v : Fin arity → Semiterm L ξ n) : Semiterm L ξ n :=
  Rew.substs v (Rew.emb o.term)

@[coe] abbrev const (c : Const L) : Semiterm L ξ n := c.operator ![]

instance : Coe (Const L) (Semiterm L ξ n) := ⟨Operator.const⟩

def comp (o : Operator L k) (w : Fin k → Operator L l) : Operator L l :=
  ⟨o.operator (fun x => (w x).term)⟩

@[simp] lemma operator_comp (o : Operator L k) (w : Fin k → Operator L l) (v : Fin l → Semiterm L ξ n) :
  (o.comp w).operator v = o.operator (fun x => (w x).operator v) := by
    simp [operator, comp, ←Rew.comp_app]; congr 1
    ext <;> simp [Rew.comp_app]; contradiction

def bvar (x : Fin n) : Operator L n := ⟨#x⟩

lemma operator_bvar (x : Fin k) (v : Fin k → Semiterm L ξ n) : (bvar x).operator v = v x := by
  simp [operator, bvar]

lemma bv_operator {k} (o : Operator L k) (v : Fin k → Semiterm L ξ (n + 1)) :
    (o.operator v).bv = .biUnion o.term.bv fun i ↦ (v i).bv  := by
  simp [operator]
  generalize o.term = s
  induction s <;> try simp [Rew.func, bv_func, Finset.biUnion_biUnion, *]
  case fvar => contradiction

lemma positive_operator_iff {k} {o : Operator L k} {v : Fin k → Semiterm L ξ (n + 1)} :
    (o.operator v).Positive ↔ ∀ i ∈ o.term.bv, (v i).Positive := by
  simp [Positive, bv_operator]
  exact ⟨fun h i hi x hx ↦ h x i hi hx, fun h x i hi hx ↦ h i hi x hx⟩

@[simp] lemma positive_const (c : Const L) : (c : Semiterm L ξ (n + 1)).Positive := by simp [const, positive_operator_iff]

-- f.operator ![ ... f.operator ![f.operator ![z, t 0], t 1], ... ,t (n-1)]
def foldr (f : Operator L 2) (z : Operator L k) : List (Operator L k) → Operator L k
  | []      => z
  | o :: os => f.comp ![foldr f z os, o]

@[simp] lemma foldr_nil (f : Operator L 2) (z : Operator L k) : f.foldr z [] = z := rfl

@[simp] lemma operator_foldr_cons (f : Operator L 2) (z : Operator L k) (o : Operator L k) (os : List (Operator L k))
  (v : Fin k → Semiterm L ξ n) :
    (f.foldr z (o :: os)).operator v = f.operator ![(f.foldr z os).operator v, o.operator v] := by
  simp [foldr, operator_comp, Matrix.fun_eq_vec₂]

def iterr (f : Operator L 2) (z : Const L) : (n : ℕ) → Operator L n
  | 0     => z
  | _ + 1 => f.foldr (bvar 0) (List.ofFn fun x => bvar x.succ)

@[simp] lemma iterr_zero (f : Operator L 2) (z : Const L) : f.iterr z 0 = z := rfl

rag.name: Nat.Primrec'.encode
rag.content:
protected theorem encode : ∀ {n}, @Primrec' n encode
  | 0 => (const 0).of_eq fun v => by rw [v.eq_nil]; rfl
  | _ + 1 =>
    (succ.comp₁ _ (natPair.comp₂ _ head (tail Primrec'.encode))).of_eq fun ⟨_ :: _, _⟩ => rfl

rag.name: Nat.Primrec'.of_prim
rag.content:
theorem of_prim {n f} : Primrec f → @Primrec' n f :=
  suffices ∀ f, Nat.Primrec f → @Primrec' 1 fun v => f v.head from fun hf =>
    (pred.comp₁ _ <|
          (this _ hf).comp₁ (fun m => Encodable.encode <| (@decode (List.Vector ℕ n) _ m).map f)
            Primrec'.encode).of_eq
      fun i => by simp [encodek]
  fun f hf => by
  induction hf with
  | zero => exact const 0
  | succ => exact succ
  | left => exact unpair₁ head
  | right => exact unpair₂ head
  | pair _ _ hf hg => exact natPair.comp₂ _ hf hg
  | comp _ _ hf hg => exact hf.comp₁ _ hg
  | prec _ _ hf hg =>
    simpa using
      prec' (unpair₂ head) (hf.comp₁ _ (unpair₁ head))
        (hg.comp₁ _ <|
          natPair.comp₂ _ (unpair₁ <| tail <| tail head) (natPair.comp₂ _ head (tail head)))

rag.content:
/-- A `Primcodable` type is an `Encodable` type for which
  the encode/decode functions are primitive recursive. -/
class Primcodable (α : Type*) extends Encodable α where
  -- Porting note: was `prim [] `.

  prim : Nat.Primrec fun n => Encodable.encode (decode n)

informal_statement: Given a type α that supports the operations Zero, One, and Add, the function of encoding an operator L into a Goedel number over α is simply the application of the encode function to L.
informal_proof:
First, we consider the type α, which possesses the operations Zero, One, and Add, indicating its capacity for zero, one, and addition operations.

Next, we focus on the operator L, which we aim to encode into a Goedel number. The encode function is designed to take such operators and represent them as natural numbers, facilitating their manipulation within formal systems.

Given the function of encoding, the Goedel number of the operator L over α is obtained by directly applying the encode function to L. Thus, the Goedel number representation of L is precisely the result of encoding L.

This demonstrates that for any type α equipped with Zero, One, and Add operations, the function used to encode operators into Goedel numbers produces results equivalent to applying the encode function to the operator itself.

import Foundation.FirstOrder.Basic.Semantics.Semantics
import Foundation.Vorspiel.NotationClass

namespace LO

namespace FirstOrder

variable {L : Language}

namespace Semiterm

structure Operator (L : Language) (n : ℕ) where
  term : Semiterm L Empty n

abbrev Const (L : Language.{u}) := Operator L 0

def fn {k} (f : L.Func k) : Operator L k := ⟨Semiterm.func f (#·)⟩

namespace Operator

def equiv : Operator L n ≃ Semiterm L Empty n where
  toFun := Operator.term
  invFun := Operator.mk
  left_inv := by intro _; simp
  right_inv := by intro _; simp

def operator {arity : ℕ} (o : Operator L arity) (v : Fin arity → Semiterm L ξ n) : Semiterm L ξ n :=
  Rew.substs v (Rew.emb o.term)

@[coe] abbrev const (c : Const L) : Semiterm L ξ n := c.operator ![]

instance : Coe (Const L) (Semiterm L ξ n) := ⟨Operator.const⟩

def comp (o : Operator L k) (w : Fin k → Operator L l) : Operator L l :=
  ⟨o.operator (fun x => (w x).term)⟩

@[simp] lemma operator_comp (o : Operator L k) (w : Fin k → Operator L l) (v : Fin l → Semiterm L ξ n) :
  (o.comp w).operator v = o.operator (fun x => (w x).operator v) := by
    simp [operator, comp, ←Rew.comp_app]; congr 1
    ext <;> simp [Rew.comp_app]; contradiction

def bvar (x : Fin n) : Operator L n := ⟨#x⟩

lemma operator_bvar (x : Fin k) (v : Fin k → Semiterm L ξ n) : (bvar x).operator v = v x := by
  simp [operator, bvar]

lemma bv_operator {k} (o : Operator L k) (v : Fin k → Semiterm L ξ (n + 1)) :
    (o.operator v).bv = .biUnion o.term.bv fun i ↦ (v i).bv  := by
  simp [operator]
  generalize o.term = s
  induction s <;> try simp [Rew.func, bv_func, Finset.biUnion_biUnion, *]
  case fvar => contradiction

lemma positive_operator_iff {k} {o : Operator L k} {v : Fin k → Semiterm L ξ (n + 1)} :
    (o.operator v).Positive ↔ ∀ i ∈ o.term.bv, (v i).Positive := by
  simp [Positive, bv_operator]
  exact ⟨fun h i hi x hx ↦ h x i hi hx, fun h x i hi hx ↦ h i hi x hx⟩

@[simp] lemma positive_const (c : Const L) : (c : Semiterm L ξ (n + 1)).Positive := by simp [const, positive_operator_iff]

-- f.operator ![ ... f.operator ![f.operator ![z, t 0], t 1], ... ,t (n-1)]
def foldr (f : Operator L 2) (z : Operator L k) : List (Operator L k) → Operator L k
  | []      => z
  | o :: os => f.comp ![foldr f z os, o]

@[simp] lemma foldr_nil (f : Operator L 2) (z : Operator L k) : f.foldr z [] = z := rfl

@[simp] lemma operator_foldr_cons (f : Operator L 2) (z : Operator L k) (o : Operator L k) (os : List (Operator L k))
  (v : Fin k → Semiterm L ξ n) :
    (f.foldr z (o :: os)).operator v = f.operator ![(f.foldr z os).operator v, o.operator v] := by
  simp [foldr, operator_comp, Matrix.fun_eq_vec₂]

def iterr (f : Operator L 2) (z : Const L) : (n : ℕ) → Operator L n
  | 0     => z
  | _ + 1 => f.foldr (bvar 0) (List.ofFn fun x => bvar x.succ)

@[simp] lemma iterr_zero (f : Operator L 2) (z : Const L) : f.iterr z 0 = z := rfl

import Foundation.FirstOrder.Basic.Semantics.Semantics
import Foundation.Vorspiel.NotationClass

namespace LO

namespace FirstOrder

variable {L : Language}

namespace Semiterm

structure Operator (L : Language) (n : ℕ) where
  term : Semiterm L Empty n

abbrev Const (L : Language.{u}) := Operator L 0

def fn {k} (f : L.Func k) : Operator L k := ⟨Semiterm.func f (#·)⟩

namespace Operator

def equiv : Operator L n ≃ Semiterm L Empty n where
  toFun := Operator.term
  invFun := Operator.mk
  left_inv := by intro _; simp
  right_inv := by intro _; simp

def operator {arity : ℕ} (o : Operator L arity) (v : Fin arity → Semiterm L ξ n) : Semiterm L ξ n :=
  Rew.substs v (Rew.emb o.term)

@[coe] abbrev const (c : Const L) : Semiterm L ξ n := c.operator ![]

instance : Coe (Const L) (Semiterm L ξ n) := ⟨Operator.const⟩

def comp (o : Operator L k) (w : Fin k → Operator L l) : Operator L l :=
  ⟨o.operator (fun x => (w x).term)⟩

@[simp] lemma operator_comp (o : Operator L k) (w : Fin k → Operator L l) (v : Fin l → Semiterm L ξ n) :
  (o.comp w).operator v = o.operator (fun x => (w x).operator v) := by
    simp [operator, comp, ←Rew.comp_app]; congr 1
    ext <;> simp [Rew.comp_app]; contradiction

def bvar (x : Fin n) : Operator L n := ⟨#x⟩

lemma operator_bvar (x : Fin k) (v : Fin k → Semiterm L ξ n) : (bvar x).operator v = v x := by
  simp [operator, bvar]

lemma bv_operator {k} (o : Operator L k) (v : Fin k → Semiterm L ξ (n + 1)) :
    (o.operator v).bv = .biUnion o.term.bv fun i ↦ (v i).bv  := by
  simp [operator]
  generalize o.term = s
  induction s <;> try simp [Rew.func, bv_func, Finset.biUnion_biUnion, *]
  case fvar => contradiction

lemma positive_operator_iff {k} {o : Operator L k} {v : Fin k → Semiterm L ξ (n + 1)} :
    (o.operator v).Positive ↔ ∀ i ∈ o.term.bv, (v i).Positive := by
  simp [Positive, bv_operator]
  exact ⟨fun h i hi x hx ↦ h x i hi hx, fun h x i hi hx ↦ h i hi x hx⟩

@[simp] lemma positive_const (c : Const L) : (c : Semiterm L ξ (n + 1)).Positive := by simp [const, positive_operator_iff]

-- f.operator ![ ... f.operator ![f.operator ![z, t 0], t 1], ... ,t (n-1)]
def foldr (f : Operator L 2) (z : Operator L k) : List (Operator L k) → Operator L k
  | []      => z
  | o :: os => f.comp ![foldr f z os, o]

@[simp] lemma foldr_nil (f : Operator L 2) (z : Operator L k) : f.foldr z [] = z := rfl

@[simp] lemma operator_foldr_cons (f : Operator L 2) (z : Operator L k) (o : Operator L k) (os : List (Operator L k))
  (v : Fin k → Semiterm L ξ n) :
    (f.foldr z (o :: os)).operator v = f.operator ![(f.foldr z os).operator v, o.operator v] := by
  simp [foldr, operator_comp, Matrix.fun_eq_vec₂]

def iterr (f : Operator L 2) (z : Const L) : (n : ℕ) → Operator L n
  | 0     => z
  | _ + 1 => f.foldr (bvar 0) (List.ofFn fun x => bvar x.succ)

@[simp] lemma iterr_zero (f : Operator L 2) (z : Const L) : f.iterr z 0 = z := rfl

informal_statement: For a term \( t \) in a given language \( L \) and a natural number \( k \), the operator \( \operatorname{npow}(L, k) \) applied to \( t \) is positive if and only if \( k \) is zero or \( t \) itself is positive.
informal_proof:
First, consider the case where \( k = 0 \). By definition, the operator \( \operatorname{npow}(L, 0) \) acts as the identity operator, meaning \( \operatorname{npow}(L, 0)[t] = t \). If \( k = 0 \), then \( \operatorname{npow}(L, 0)[t] \) is positive because \( t \) is positive by assumption.

Next, consider the case where \( k > 0 \). Here, the operator \( \operatorname{npow}(L, k) \) is applied to the term \( t \), and its positivity depends on the positivity of \( t \). By the definition of the operator \( \operatorname{npow} \), if \( t \) is positive, then \( \operatorname{npow}(L, k)[t] \) will also be positive. If \( t \) were not positive, then \( \operatorname{npow}(L, k)[t] \) would not be positive either, as the positivity is preserved through the application of the operator when \( k > 0 \).

Since these are the only two possibilities for \( k \) (either \( k = 0 \) or \( k > 0 \)), the equivalence holds: \( \operatorname{npow}(L, k)[t] \) is positive if and only if \( k = 0 \) or \( t \) is positive.

import Foundation.FirstOrder.Basic.Semantics.Semantics
import Foundation.Vorspiel.NotationClass

namespace LO

namespace FirstOrder

variable {L : Language}

namespace Semiterm

structure Operator (L : Language) (n : ℕ) where
  term : Semiterm L Empty n

abbrev Const (L : Language.{u}) := Operator L 0

def fn {k} (f : L.Func k) : Operator L k := ⟨Semiterm.func f (#·)⟩

namespace Operator

def equiv : Operator L n ≃ Semiterm L Empty n where
  toFun := Operator.term
  invFun := Operator.mk
  left_inv := by intro _; simp
  right_inv := by intro _; simp

def operator {arity : ℕ} (o : Operator L arity) (v : Fin arity → Semiterm L ξ n) : Semiterm L ξ n :=
  Rew.substs v (Rew.emb o.term)

@[coe] abbrev const (c : Const L) : Semiterm L ξ n := c.operator ![]

instance : Coe (Const L) (Semiterm L ξ n) := ⟨Operator.const⟩

def comp (o : Operator L k) (w : Fin k → Operator L l) : Operator L l :=
  ⟨o.operator (fun x => (w x).term)⟩

@[simp] lemma operator_comp (o : Operator L k) (w : Fin k → Operator L l) (v : Fin l → Semiterm L ξ n) :
  (o.comp w).operator v = o.operator (fun x => (w x).operator v) := by
    simp [operator, comp, ←Rew.comp_app]; congr 1
    ext <;> simp [Rew.comp_app]; contradiction

def bvar (x : Fin n) : Operator L n := ⟨#x⟩

lemma operator_bvar (x : Fin k) (v : Fin k → Semiterm L ξ n) : (bvar x).operator v = v x := by
  simp [operator, bvar]

lemma bv_operator {k} (o : Operator L k) (v : Fin k → Semiterm L ξ (n + 1)) :
    (o.operator v).bv = .biUnion o.term.bv fun i ↦ (v i).bv  := by
  simp [operator]
  generalize o.term = s
  induction s <;> try simp [Rew.func, bv_func, Finset.biUnion_biUnion, *]
  case fvar => contradiction

lemma positive_operator_iff {k} {o : Operator L k} {v : Fin k → Semiterm L ξ (n + 1)} :
    (o.operator v).Positive ↔ ∀ i ∈ o.term.bv, (v i).Positive := by
  simp [Positive, bv_operator]
  exact ⟨fun h i hi x hx ↦ h x i hi hx, fun h x i hi hx ↦ h i hi x hx⟩

@[simp] lemma positive_const (c : Const L) : (c : Semiterm L ξ (n + 1)).Positive := by simp [const, positive_operator_iff]

-- f.operator ![ ... f.operator ![f.operator ![z, t 0], t 1], ... ,t (n-1)]
def foldr (f : Operator L 2) (z : Operator L k) : List (Operator L k) → Operator L k
  | []      => z
  | o :: os => f.comp ![foldr f z os, o]

@[simp] lemma foldr_nil (f : Operator L 2) (z : Operator L k) : f.foldr z [] = z := rfl

@[simp] lemma operator_foldr_cons (f : Operator L 2) (z : Operator L k) (o : Operator L k) (os : List (Operator L k))
  (v : Fin k → Semiterm L ξ n) :
    (f.foldr z (o :: os)).operator v = f.operator ![(f.foldr z os).operator v, o.operator v] := by
  simp [foldr, operator_comp, Matrix.fun_eq_vec₂]

def iterr (f : Operator L 2) (z : Const L) : (n : ℕ) → Operator L n
  | 0     => z
  | _ + 1 => f.foldr (bvar 0) (List.ofFn fun x => bvar x.succ)

@[simp] lemma iterr_zero (f : Operator L 2) (z : Const L) : f.iterr z 0 = z := rfl

informal_statement: For any type \( L \) and any natural number \( n \), the polynomial \( L^{n+1} \) is equal to the multiplication of \( L^n \) with the base variable \( bvar\, 0 \).
informal_proof: In the definition of \( npow \), it is established that \( npow\, L\, (n + 1) \) is recursively defined as the product of \( npow\, L\, n \) and \( bvar\, 0 \). By the very definition of \( npow \), this recursive application directly yields the equality \( npow\, L\, (n + 1) = \mul \circ \| [npow\, L\, n, bvar\, 0] \| \). Hence, the equality holds due to the recursive definition of \( npow \), making the statement trivially true by reflexivity of equality.

import Foundation.FirstOrder.Basic.Semantics.Semantics
import Foundation.Vorspiel.NotationClass

namespace LO

namespace FirstOrder

variable {L : Language}

namespace Semiterm

structure Operator (L : Language) (n : ℕ) where
  term : Semiterm L Empty n

abbrev Const (L : Language.{u}) := Operator L 0

def fn {k} (f : L.Func k) : Operator L k := ⟨Semiterm.func f (#·)⟩

namespace Operator

def equiv : Operator L n ≃ Semiterm L Empty n where
  toFun := Operator.term
  invFun := Operator.mk
  left_inv := by intro _; simp
  right_inv := by intro _; simp

def operator {arity : ℕ} (o : Operator L arity) (v : Fin arity → Semiterm L ξ n) : Semiterm L ξ n :=
  Rew.substs v (Rew.emb o.term)

@[coe] abbrev const (c : Const L) : Semiterm L ξ n := c.operator ![]

instance : Coe (Const L) (Semiterm L ξ n) := ⟨Operator.const⟩

def comp (o : Operator L k) (w : Fin k → Operator L l) : Operator L l :=
  ⟨o.operator (fun x => (w x).term)⟩

@[simp] lemma operator_comp (o : Operator L k) (w : Fin k → Operator L l) (v : Fin l → Semiterm L ξ n) :
  (o.comp w).operator v = o.operator (fun x => (w x).operator v) := by
    simp [operator, comp, ←Rew.comp_app]; congr 1
    ext <;> simp [Rew.comp_app]; contradiction

def bvar (x : Fin n) : Operator L n := ⟨#x⟩

lemma operator_bvar (x : Fin k) (v : Fin k → Semiterm L ξ n) : (bvar x).operator v = v x := by
  simp [operator, bvar]

lemma bv_operator {k} (o : Operator L k) (v : Fin k → Semiterm L ξ (n + 1)) :
    (o.operator v).bv = .biUnion o.term.bv fun i ↦ (v i).bv  := by
  simp [operator]
  generalize o.term = s
  induction s <;> try simp [Rew.func, bv_func, Finset.biUnion_biUnion, *]
  case fvar => contradiction

lemma positive_operator_iff {k} {o : Operator L k} {v : Fin k → Semiterm L ξ (n + 1)} :
    (o.operator v).Positive ↔ ∀ i ∈ o.term.bv, (v i).Positive := by
  simp [Positive, bv_operator]
  exact ⟨fun h i hi x hx ↦ h x i hi hx, fun h x i hi hx ↦ h i hi x hx⟩

@[simp] lemma positive_const (c : Const L) : (c : Semiterm L ξ (n + 1)).Positive := by simp [const, positive_operator_iff]

-- f.operator ![ ... f.operator ![f.operator ![z, t 0], t 1], ... ,t (n-1)]
def foldr (f : Operator L 2) (z : Operator L k) : List (Operator L k) → Operator L k
  | []      => z
  | o :: os => f.comp ![foldr f z os, o]

@[simp] lemma foldr_nil (f : Operator L 2) (z : Operator L k) : f.foldr z [] = z := rfl

@[simp] lemma operator_foldr_cons (f : Operator L 2) (z : Operator L k) (o : Operator L k) (os : List (Operator L k))
  (v : Fin k → Semiterm L ξ n) :
    (f.foldr z (o :: os)).operator v = f.operator ![(f.foldr z os).operator v, o.operator v] := by
  simp [foldr, operator_comp, Matrix.fun_eq_vec₂]

def iterr (f : Operator L 2) (z : Const L) : (n : ℕ) → Operator L n
  | 0     => z
  | _ + 1 => f.foldr (bvar 0) (List.ofFn fun x => bvar x.succ)

@[simp] lemma iterr_zero (f : Operator L 2) (z : Const L) : f.iterr z 0 = z := rfl

import Foundation.FirstOrder.Basic.Semantics.Semantics
import Foundation.Vorspiel.NotationClass

namespace LO

namespace FirstOrder

variable {L : Language}

namespace Semiterm

structure Operator (L : Language) (n : ℕ) where
  term : Semiterm L Empty n

abbrev Const (L : Language.{u}) := Operator L 0

def fn {k} (f : L.Func k) : Operator L k := ⟨Semiterm.func f (#·)⟩

namespace Operator

def equiv : Operator L n ≃ Semiterm L Empty n where
  toFun := Operator.term
  invFun := Operator.mk
  left_inv := by intro _; simp
  right_inv := by intro _; simp

def operator {arity : ℕ} (o : Operator L arity) (v : Fin arity → Semiterm L ξ n) : Semiterm L ξ n :=
  Rew.substs v (Rew.emb o.term)

@[coe] abbrev const (c : Const L) : Semiterm L ξ n := c.operator ![]

instance : Coe (Const L) (Semiterm L ξ n) := ⟨Operator.const⟩

def comp (o : Operator L k) (w : Fin k → Operator L l) : Operator L l :=
  ⟨o.operator (fun x => (w x).term)⟩

@[simp] lemma operator_comp (o : Operator L k) (w : Fin k → Operator L l) (v : Fin l → Semiterm L ξ n) :
  (o.comp w).operator v = o.operator (fun x => (w x).operator v) := by
    simp [operator, comp, ←Rew.comp_app]; congr 1
    ext <;> simp [Rew.comp_app]; contradiction

def bvar (x : Fin n) : Operator L n := ⟨#x⟩

lemma operator_bvar (x : Fin k) (v : Fin k → Semiterm L ξ n) : (bvar x).operator v = v x := by
  simp [operator, bvar]

lemma bv_operator {k} (o : Operator L k) (v : Fin k → Semiterm L ξ (n + 1)) :
    (o.operator v).bv = .biUnion o.term.bv fun i ↦ (v i).bv  := by
  simp [operator]
  generalize o.term = s
  induction s <;> try simp [Rew.func, bv_func, Finset.biUnion_biUnion, *]
  case fvar => contradiction

lemma positive_operator_iff {k} {o : Operator L k} {v : Fin k → Semiterm L ξ (n + 1)} :
    (o.operator v).Positive ↔ ∀ i ∈ o.term.bv, (v i).Positive := by
  simp [Positive, bv_operator]
  exact ⟨fun h i hi x hx ↦ h x i hi hx, fun h x i hi hx ↦ h i hi x hx⟩

@[simp] lemma positive_const (c : Const L) : (c : Semiterm L ξ (n + 1)).Positive := by simp [const, positive_operator_iff]

-- f.operator ![ ... f.operator ![f.operator ![z, t 0], t 1], ... ,t (n-1)]
def foldr (f : Operator L 2) (z : Operator L k) : List (Operator L k) → Operator L k
  | []      => z
  | o :: os => f.comp ![foldr f z os, o]

@[simp] lemma foldr_nil (f : Operator L 2) (z : Operator L k) : f.foldr z [] = z := rfl

@[simp] lemma operator_foldr_cons (f : Operator L 2) (z : Operator L k) (o : Operator L k) (os : List (Operator L k))
  (v : Fin k → Semiterm L ξ n) :
    (f.foldr z (o :: os)).operator v = f.operator ![(f.foldr z os).operator v, o.operator v] := by
  simp [foldr, operator_comp, Matrix.fun_eq_vec₂]

def iterr (f : Operator L 2) (z : Const L) : (n : ℕ) → Operator L n
  | 0     => z
  | _ + 1 => f.foldr (bvar 0) (List.ofFn fun x => bvar x.succ)

@[simp] lemma iterr_zero (f : Operator L 2) (z : Const L) : f.iterr z 0 = z := rfl

/-- An auxiliary lemma that can be used to prove `⇑(f ^ n) = ⇑f^[n]`. -/
@[to_additive]
lemma hom_coe_pow {F : Type*} [Monoid F] (c : F → M → M) (h1 : c 1 = id)
    (hmul : ∀ f g, c (f * g) = c f ∘ c g) (f : F) : ∀ n, c (f ^ n) = (c f)^[n]
  | 0 => by
    rw [pow_zero, h1]
    rfl
  | n + 1 => by rw [pow_succ, iterate_succ, hmul, hom_coe_pow c h1 hmul f n]

informal_statement: The function f, which represents the nth power of a language's indicative, preserves structure such that applying it to the combination of two languages is equivalent to combining the results of applying f to each language individually.
informal_proof:
To establish that f is a homomorphism, we must show that for any two languages A and B, f(A ⊕ B) = f(A) ⊕ f(B). 

First, consider that ⊕ denotes the operation of combining two languages, and f(L) represents the nth power of the indicative for language L. The nth power implies the operation is applied sequentially n times.

Given that f is defined as a multiplicative function over the language, meaning it combines results multiplicatively, we analyze the behavior under combination:

1. By definition, f(A) represents the result of applying the operator n times to language A.
2. Similarly, f(B) is the result for language B.
3. When combining A and B, the operator ⊕ is applied once to the combined language A ⊕ B.
4. Since f is a multiplicative operator applied n times, f(A ⊕ B) captures the complete structure of ⊕ acting on the combined system.
5. On the other hand, f(A) ⊕ f(B) represents combining n- applications of the operator on A with n- applications on B.

By induction on n:
- Base case (n=1): f(A ⊕ B) = f(A) ⊕ f(B), which trivially holds as they represent the same operation.
- Inductive step: Assume true for n=k; then for n=k+1, f(A ⊕ B) being a multiplicative extension ensures it aligns with f(A) ⊕ f(B).

Thus, f maintains the structure under combination, confirming it as a homomorphism.

variable {L : Language}

structure Operator (L : Language) (n : ℕ) where

abbrev Const (L : Language.{u}) := Operator L 0

def fn {k} (f : L.Func k) : Operator L k := ⟨Semiterm.func f (#·)⟩

namespace Operator

def equiv : Operator L n ≃ Semiterm L Empty n where
  toFun := Operator.term
  invFun := Operator.mk
  left_inv := by intro _; simp
  right_inv := by intro _; simp

def operator {arity : ℕ} (o : Operator L arity) (v : Fin arity → Semiterm L ξ n) : Semiterm L ξ n :=
  Rew.substs v (Rew.emb o.term)

@[coe] abbrev const (c : Const L) : Semiterm L ξ n := c.operator ![]

instance : Coe (Const L) (Semiterm L ξ n) := ⟨Operator.const⟩

def comp (o : Operator L k) (w : Fin k → Operator L l) : Operator L l :=
  ⟨o.operator (fun x => (w x).term)⟩

@[simp] lemma operator_comp (o : Operator L k) (w : Fin k → Operator L l) (v : Fin l → Semiterm L ξ n) :
  (o.comp w).operator v = o.operator (fun x => (w x).operator v) := by
    simp [operator, comp, ←Rew.comp_app]; congr 1
    ext <;> simp [Rew.comp_app]; contradiction

def bvar (x : Fin n) : Operator L n := ⟨#x⟩

lemma operator_bvar (x : Fin k) (v : Fin k → Semiterm L ξ n) : (bvar x).operator v = v x := by
  simp [operator, bvar]

lemma bv_operator {k} (o : Operator L k) (v : Fin k → Semiterm L ξ (n + 1)) :
    (o.operator v).bv = .biUnion o.term.bv fun i ↦ (v i).bv  := by
  simp [operator]
  generalize o.term = s
  induction s <;> try simp [Rew.func, bv_func, Finset.biUnion_biUnion, *]
  case fvar => contradiction

lemma positive_operator_iff {k} {o : Operator L k} {v : Fin k → Semiterm L ξ (n + 1)} :
    (o.operator v).Positive ↔ ∀ i ∈ o.term.bv, (v i).Positive := by
  simp [Positive, bv_operator]
  exact ⟨fun h i hi x hx ↦ h x i hi hx, fun h x i hi hx ↦ h i hi x hx⟩

@[simp] lemma positive_const (c : Const L) : (c : Semiterm L ξ (n + 1)).Positive := by simp [const, positive_operator_iff]

-- f.operator ![ ... f.operator ![f.operator ![z, t 0], t 1], ... ,t (n-1)]
def foldr (f : Operator L 2) (z : Operator L k) : List (Operator L k) → Operator L k
  | []      => z
  | o :: os => f.comp ![foldr f z os, o]

@[simp] lemma foldr_nil (f : Operator L 2) (z : Operator L k) : f.foldr z [] = z := rfl

@[simp] lemma operator_foldr_cons (f : Operator L 2) (z : Operator L k) (o : Operator L k) (os : List (Operator L k))
  (v : Fin k → Semiterm L ξ n) :
    (f.foldr z (o :: os)).operator v = f.operator ![(f.foldr z os).operator v, o.operator v] := by
  simp [foldr, operator_comp, Matrix.fun_eq_vec₂]

  | 0     => z
  | _ + 1 => f.foldr (bvar 0) (List.ofFn fun x => bvar x.succ)

@[simp] lemma iterr_zero (f : Operator L 2) (z : Const L) : f.iterr z 0 = z := rfl

Specifically, the Exp.positive_iff lemma directly provides the necessary conditions, and through simplification, we conclude that the positivity of the exp operator applied to $t$ necessarily aligns with the positivity of $t$ itself.

import Foundation.FirstOrder.Basic.Semantics.Semantics
import Foundation.Vorspiel.NotationClass

namespace LO

namespace FirstOrder

variable {L : Language}

namespace Semiterm

structure Operator (L : Language) (n : ℕ) where
  term : Semiterm L Empty n

abbrev Const (L : Language.{u}) := Operator L 0

def fn {k} (f : L.Func k) : Operator L k := ⟨Semiterm.func f (#·)⟩

namespace Operator

def equiv : Operator L n ≃ Semiterm L Empty n where
  toFun := Operator.term
  invFun := Operator.mk
  left_inv := by intro _; simp
  right_inv := by intro _; simp

def operator {arity : ℕ} (o : Operator L arity) (v : Fin arity → Semiterm L ξ n) : Semiterm L ξ n :=
  Rew.substs v (Rew.emb o.term)

@[coe] abbrev const (c : Const L) : Semiterm L ξ n := c.operator ![]

instance : Coe (Const L) (Semiterm L ξ n) := ⟨Operator.const⟩

def comp (o : Operator L k) (w : Fin k → Operator L l) : Operator L l :=
  ⟨o.operator (fun x => (w x).term)⟩

@[simp] lemma operator_comp (o : Operator L k) (w : Fin k → Operator L l) (v : Fin l → Semiterm L ξ n) :
  (o.comp w).operator v = o.operator (fun x => (w x).operator v) := by
    simp [operator, comp, ←Rew.comp_app]; congr 1
    ext <;> simp [Rew.comp_app]; contradiction

def bvar (x : Fin n) : Operator L n := ⟨#x⟩

lemma operator_bvar (x : Fin k) (v : Fin k → Semiterm L ξ n) : (bvar x).operator v = v x := by
  simp [operator, bvar]

lemma bv_operator {k} (o : Operator L k) (v : Fin k → Semiterm L ξ (n + 1)) :
    (o.operator v).bv = .biUnion o.term.bv fun i ↦ (v i).bv  := by
  simp [operator]
  generalize o.term = s
  induction s <;> try simp [Rew.func, bv_func, Finset.biUnion_biUnion, *]
  case fvar => contradiction

lemma positive_operator_iff {k} {o : Operator L k} {v : Fin k → Semiterm L ξ (n + 1)} :
    (o.operator v).Positive ↔ ∀ i ∈ o.term.bv, (v i).Positive := by
  simp [Positive, bv_operator]
  exact ⟨fun h i hi x hx ↦ h x i hi hx, fun h x i hi hx ↦ h i hi x hx⟩

@[simp] lemma positive_const (c : Const L) : (c : Semiterm L ξ (n + 1)).Positive := by simp [const, positive_operator_iff]

-- f.operator ![ ... f.operator ![f.operator ![z, t 0], t 1], ... ,t (n-1)]
def foldr (f : Operator L 2) (z : Operator L k) : List (Operator L k) → Operator L k
  | []      => z
  | o :: os => f.comp ![foldr f z os, o]

@[simp] lemma foldr_nil (f : Operator L 2) (z : Operator L k) : f.foldr z [] = z := rfl

@[simp] lemma operator_foldr_cons (f : Operator L 2) (z : Operator L k) (o : Operator L k) (os : List (Operator L k))
  (v : Fin k → Semiterm L ξ n) :
    (f.foldr z (o :: os)).operator v = f.operator ![(f.foldr z os).operator v, o.operator v] := by
  simp [foldr, operator_comp, Matrix.fun_eq_vec₂]

def iterr (f : Operator L 2) (z : Const L) : (n : ℕ) → Operator L n
  | 0     => z
  | _ + 1 => f.foldr (bvar 0) (List.ofFn fun x => bvar x.succ)

@[simp] lemma iterr_zero (f : Operator L 2) (z : Const L) : f.iterr z 0 = z := rfl
